notes.title: Units in Fight for Freedom #5
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/42379a62a6b754c9a1c06f2e5f0a87ab66750249.png

The screaming Stuka remains one of the most recognizable images of the Second World War. They were as much of a sensation at the time - faced with the enemy dive bombers, the British immediately wanted their own.

American-made A-31 Vengeance had all the weaknesses of a dive bomber - a dire need for a fighter escort, and a reliance on local air superiority - but made up for them by being rugged, dependable and, according to some accounts, simply “a lovely aircraft to fly”. They did not fare well in the battle of Britain, but won their glory in Burma, where, safe from overwhelming flak fire, Vengeances were used to conduct numerous bombing raids on the Japanese supply lines and military infrastructure.

A-31 Vengeance Mk. I was the first model ordered, with the initial order of 200. A-31 Vengeance Mk. II had only minor differences, while A-35B Vengeance Mk. IV boasted a more powerful engine, and an increased bomb load.

A-31 Vengeance Mk. I
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/a273efd078e725f4f904673128da31e6fbb60aa9.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/0ec1dedd720d97fc0c3e2085f6f387cbd7d0724c.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/6fab56984cc67f889834f74afb296ea759641d66.jpg

A-31 Vengeance Mk. II
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/aa50394773fc6bf1fc0615526370859df57895ae.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/eb6f18edea0f203dc3896f11ea25d04f20b51107.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/9809abc6b22e9c54f35cafa27765bcb4e80b2890.jpg

A-35B Vengeance Mk. IV
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/9a1c47e3caca2dd78c903b2235f4f94a3224955c.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/ee6e0b5a690b349f0b991c40cf78fbce46f36dcf.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38607672/98027904a606efd32c0a711e2fe631f035573d29.jpg

In the game
The Vengeance series will be the only Dive bombers available in the UK campaign. Unlike ordinary Tactical bombers, Dive bombers deal mostly Lethal damage, not allowing the enemy to restore wounded at the end of its turn. Thus, it is more effective if you want to deal permanent damage to the enemy troops. Although, other bombers that deal mostly Nonlethal damage, could be better for making the enemy surrender and taking prisoners, instead of outright annihilating the enemy troops.

notes.title: Units in Fight for Freedom #4
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/757788aa606421ee2c085579471b480b77de4047.jpg

Unlike the sluggish and heavily-armored infantry tanks, the concept of “cruiser tanks” was designed around speed and mobility. In many ways these are the UK’s answer to the Pz III, with equivalent armaments and similar overall performance. Some early “close support” variants even came armed with a howitzer, fulfilling the combat role of an assault gun.

The Cruiser Mk III A13 was built for speed and armed with a QF 2-pounder. It was designed to swarm the enemy, and had poor armor - something the crew had to be mindful of.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/7e5904557a1bd2e877b4ad7d2d4cce48800972da.jpg

Cruiser Mk IV was a hasty course correction - so hasty many models were shipped straight to the frontline, often with some parts missing. It fared poorly against thick German armor, but quickly became a soldiers’ favorite in Africa, where its speed and good climate adaptation made it deadly when facing lightly armored Italian tanks.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/aa2afd0d82b447d0445a5c6333b4a9571ebb8a89.jpg

Crusader II kept the speed and the 2-pounder cannon, but boasted additional protective panels on its sides, and much thicker front armor, offset by the powerful Nuffield Liberty Mk.III engine. This machine came into use in 1942, just in time for the major battles in North Africa.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/cbf33103288253bc261dea04eb0c56838c7608e9.jpg
In the game
The сruiser tanks’ high mobility is reflected by the high movement points, but their defense is mediocre. Still, it is a force to be reckoned with, especially early into the war. Their armament provides decent Soft attack and mediocre Hard attack capabilities.

notes.title: Starni Games 2020 report
notes.content:
Hello, guys! There are many opinions about the year 2020. Many think it was a bad and troublesome year. Some think 2021 will be even worse. We do not think, we make games. So, we will tell you about all the events happening with Starni Games in 2020, and let you make your own conclusions.

Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg release
We have started to work on Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg back in 2019, right after The Pacific release. Yet the majority of the work was done in 2020. It was tough to meet the deadliner, but we did it despite all the troubles. The release was a success, and the game is doing reasonably well. 

Big Battle: pandemic vs release 
We had to work remotely in April and May 2020, just before the Blitzkrieg release. Then we got back to the office, but in October went remote again for a month. Overall, working remotely and doing Mocap and VO mid-pandemic was quite challenging. If you want to know more about it make sure to check out our Developer’s Diaries dedicated to these issues.

Russian government stops the Blitzkrieg
Soon after the Blitzkrieg release, the Russian government demanded that Steam remove it from the store in Russia. Moreover, the spokesman of the Russian president commented on it. They even claimed to file an official investigation request to the UN. If you want to find out more about the issue, make sure to check our news about it.

Free game Demo
This year we started to create free Demo versions for our games, to make sure you can try them out before buying. We want to make sure that you know what you get.

👉Check out our latest Demo here.

However, at first, there were issues. When we submitted the Blitzkrieg Demo 3 months after we published the game, Steam blocked both the full game and the Demo. We had to start all the explanations anew. We managed to lift the limitation off of the full game, but only at the cost of creating a German-only version with Hitler’s face blurred. You can learn more about it here. 

Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism release
All the while we kept working on the Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism. The release date was planned for 13 November, and once again we had to work remotely for some time and faced some other problems. All in all, we managed to break through the enemy’s encirclement and released the game on time. It was our most polished and smooth release so far. 

Hitler is more popular than Stalin
Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism release was the least successful to date in financial terms, but the game got the highest review score so far. It sold 2 times fewer copies than Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg. However, due to other projects still showing decent results we are able to continue with the Strategic Mind series. We discuss it in more detail here. 

New Starni Games website and Starni Store
Just on the last day of the year, we managed to release our new website - starnigames.com. The design was fully reworked. It will get further polish in January. You can also buy our games (Steam keys) there directly from the developer. Yet, if you prefer to do it on steam - we are more than happy with that. You can learn more about the website and different stores here. 

Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom - the work has begun
In November and December, we were working really hard and made good progress, making a full release of our next title in Q2 2021 very realistic. So, far we have the first gameplay trailer and an early Free Demo with the first operation. We plan to update the Demo as our work progresses and release more trailers along the way. We will keep you updated on our progress through regular news and Developer’s Diaries. 

Developers Diaries
This year we started to issue Developer’s Diaries regularly and plan to keep doing so in 2021, so stay tuned. In case you missed our story so far, you can check it out here:
1. New VO and mocap setup
2. Units’ speech review. Part 1
3. Units’ speech review. Part 2
4. Strategic Mind Franchise Soundtrack
5. Undo feature, new music, and hilarious moments
6. Designing winter operations
7. 5 days after the release, new ice visuals
8. A windy road
9. Communist Economy

Developer’s Gameplay
We also started a series of Developer’s Gameplay, where our Lead Game Designer plays our games with commentary, telling you more about the game mechanics and the development process. 

[previewyoutube=out9Rh8xRvQ;full][/previewyoutube]
New episodes will be available in January 2021, so stay tuned. We want to be even more open and transparent about our production, so feel free to ask any questions you like and we will do our best to answer them in future episodes.

Wishlists matter
You may not know, but the best indicator that the game will do well is to have a high wishlist count. That is why all game developers are really happy when they get more wishlists. So, if you want to make us happier and did not add Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom to your wishlist yet, that would make a great New Year present for our whole team. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1381850/Strategic_Mind_Fight_for_Freedom/
Our power grows 
The power of Starni Games is in its team members, in their skills and expertise. When the Panzer Strategy was released there were only 3 people in the office, and a couple more remote or outsource. In 2019 the team grew from 3 to 10 people. After the Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg release we hired 3 more people. A couple more guys will join our team in January making it 15 people in the office. We hope that the team and the company overall will keep on growing in the next year and all of our plans will be carried out. 

The novelty in the Strategic Mind series and community feedback
The changes to the series were gradual, but in retrospect, there were quite a lot of changes. A large portion of them suggested by you - the player’s community. Here are some of them:
- two new classes Armored train and Assault gun
- winter operations (visuals and mechanics)
- retreat operations (gameplay and mechanics)
- better Steam integration: localization, cloud saves etc.
- Steam Achievements and Leaderboards
- lots of new skills, HQ skills, and equipment
- lots of new units for various countries
- general performance optimization
- the Undo button
- additional game settings and hotkeys
- tons of bug fixed and improvements

Strategic Mind Franchise Soundtrack
This year we started to produce our own exclusive soundtrack in cooperation with the Daraba studio. It is shared across the series. You can find it here:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1358280/Strategic_Mind_Franchise_Soundtrack/
Strategic Mind Complete Collection bundle on Steam
The Strategic Mind series is growing and we decided to provide an opportunity to save some money on getting additional titles, especially for our long-time community members. So, now you can get all the titles you do not have at a 20% discount any time, and on top of any other discounts, which is great. We will also add the next title to the pool, so if you already have all the Strategic Mind titles, you will be able to purchase the bundle and get a nice 20% discount at the release of Strategic MInd: Fight for Freedom. 

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/16499/Strategic_Mind_Complete_Collection/
Future plans
'If you want to make God laugh, tell him about your plans.'

This year was quite challenging and unpredictable, and we do not know what to expect from the coming year 2021. Yet, we will strive to keep creating the best games we can. We cannot disclose all of our plans right now, but you will be properly informed in due time. So far, we are concentrated on delivering Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom in Q2 2021, as promised.

We wish you all a great holiday and a happy New Year! 🎄

See you in 2021 🖤

Starni Games team

notes.title: Units in Fight for Freedom #3
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38153924/fad4a6042d03a98d1f0ffc679e1dc571f6a358f8.png

The Bristol Type 156 Beaufighter, often called the Beau, was a multi-role aircraft - primarily heavy-fighter. Developed by the Bristol Aeroplane Company in the UK. It was used as a long-range heavy fighter, bomber, torpedo bomber and night fighter. 

Beaufighter was a very successful aircraft that entered the war during the Battle of Britain. It was relatively slow by fighter standards but could carry more weight, which allowed for the installation of powerful armaments and radars.

Starting late 1940 many Beaufighters were equipped with radars for night operations and proved to be a very effective counter to the German night raids. Additionally, it was often equipped with air-to-surface missiles.

In the game

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38153924/a9aa28384912e9055bfe5b5c40ac06ce13fb9dc6.png

Like other long-range fighters in the game, Beaufighter has 60 fuel instead of the usual 40. That allows it to operate across larger distances and be less conservative with skills like Afterburner or Overwatch breakthrough. In that regard, it has a similar role to the German Me-110 series. At the same time, it is better at attacking ground targets and could be used successfully in the ground attack aircraft role. You can also equip it with air-to-ground missiles.

https://media.giphy.com/media/9ggnVRTTnLgNI7GD0Z/giphy.gif

We will keep posting new units that will appear for the first time in the Strategic Mind series, so stay tuned!

notes.title: "Undo move" story contest results
notes.content:
Hello guys! Last Friday we offered you to tell us about the episode from your life best described as “I wish I had an “Undo” button”. Here is the link:
https://steamcommunity.com/games/1381850/announcements/detail/2945881487873930631
However, we put the wrong email at first and had to correct it the next day. When we realized that, we really wished we had an Undo button ;) .

The stories you sent us are much more exciting though. Thank you very much for sending us your great stories. All of them are very interesting, but we had to pick only two. It was a tough choice, but we selected the two that resonate the most with people’s feelings and make the reader feel compassion for the author. So, here are the two best stories, the authors of which will get free 'Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom keys':

Story one
Okay, well, this is a pretty funny, if not painful story, that happened to me in the third grade. So our school was pretty large and for the third grade classes, they were out in this large field away from the main buildings. (Why, I'll never really know.) So, we were quite a ways from the playground so we mostly just used the large field to play in. One day, most of the male students were all playing football, which I was a part of though my issue was that nobody was throwing me the ball even when I was wide open. Now, it's important to know that this was two-handed touch US Football, so there was no tackling of the sort, but as you can probably guess, that wasn't the case eventually. Towards the end of the recess time, the game took a hard hitting turn as I recall two brothers who were playing opposite teams from each other got into it and the whole thing collapsed into almost all the guys getting into a huge dogpile on each other. And from out of the pile came the football so I thought the play was still live and it was my first time touching the ball all recess so I grabbed it and started running towards what we designated as the endzone. I ran as fast as I could since I was so convinced everyone was behind me and trying to tackle me. I ran into the endzone without being touched and started to celebrate because I was so proud. My undo button would've been not to even grab the ball... in order to spare me from the humiliation of no one even caring that I had the ball in the first place! Everyone was still fighting each other and the teachers were trying clear up the pile! So basically, what was one of the proudest moments I ever felt, was turned into one of pure embarrassment and shame since no one even watched me or congratulated me or anything. To make matters worse, I became the most hated boy in the third grade that day since I was the only boy who didn't get banned from recess.

Story two
When I expressed love to my loved one on QQ, it was not her who logged into her account, but her girlfriend. Her girlfriend pretended to accept it herself, but then she clarified the facts and apologized to me and rejected me. If it happened again, I would never say anything without identifying her. Of course, I hope nothing happens.

notes.title: Developers' Diaries #9
notes.content:
Hello, guys! A month has passed since the Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism release and we are ready to share some insights into the financial results of the release for our company.

Bad news for Stalin
In the first two weeks since release, Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism has two times fewer copies sold and twice lower gross revenue than its predecessor Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg over the same 2-week period after release. There are a couple of possible reasons:

 End of the year clutter in November with lots of big titles being released. Although, Strategic Mind: The Pacific was more successful during the same period.
 The USSR theme is less interesting/popular than the German one. (Seems the most likely reason)
 Something else.

Games quality
One might think that the game quality was the reason, but that is not the case. The games are quite close in terms of quality and gameplay. Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism has higher Steam reviews score than Blitzkrieg - 94% positive reviews at the moment - and it was more polished at launch. Thus, in terms of quality, we can say that the bar was raised higher this time and the community feedback tells us as much. Does that mean the higher quality of the game does not directly translate into higher sales?

Wishlists comparison
Both games had very close wishlist numbers prior to the game launch. That brings us to the question, what affects the game release the most?

On the bright side
The Spectre of Communism is more popular in China and Russia. 

To be, or not to be?
Despite the unsuccessful start of Stalin’s career on Steam, we keep working on our next project Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom that is scheduled for Q2 2021. We hope that the upcoming title will gather more attention from the audience, considering that it features both US and British campaigns, as well as alternate history scenarios.

“It seems that the 5-year-plan will not be completed this time around. Bear with us, Comrades, the next 5-year-plan will most certainly be fulfilled within 4 years.”
Oleksandr Sienin, Lead game designer at Starni Games

In wishlist we trust
Despite the unsuccessful launch of the Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism, a wishlist count remains the best way to estimate the game’s potential at release and help the game get more attention on Steam.

You can support our team and help us with the future release by adding the upcoming Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom to your wishlist:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1381850/Strategic_Mind_Fight_for_Freedom/

Also, if you have missed the previous Developer’s Diaries episode, where we told you how the team went through the pandemics so far - make sure to check it out:

https://steamcommunity.com/games/1341170/announcements/detail/2934622488787841394
If you have something to say to us - make sure to leave your take on the situation in the comments below. We are always eager to get all sorts of feedback. 

Stay tuned for more Developers’ Diaries next week.

With best regards
Starni Games team

notes.title: Developers' Diaries #8
notes.content:
Hello, guys! After the launch of Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism last month, we can finally tell you a bit more about the whole process. Recently, many companies started to attribute various delays and issues to the pandemics. We will do another thing: tell you how we managed to release the game on time, despite a number of setbacks along the road. 

Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg release
The lockdown reached Kyiv in early April. We were working from the office up until the subway and other public transport ceased to function. Then we set up remote work tools and started working from home.

One of the issues was that part of Halder’s VO was unfinished, the actor doing his part lived in another city, and all trains between our cities were canceled. So, we had to ask him to record remotely and the sound was different from our usual setup.

Working from home was quite challenging, especially for people on the team who have children asking their Papa to “play with them, not do some stupid work”. So, our CEO and Lead Programmer at once Ihor Tymoshenko kept working from the office all along during this time to avoid family distractions and focus on the work.

Other people had troubles with working hours - at home, you just sleep, eat, and work, there is no boundary between “workplace” and “home”, especially prior to release. Yet we have managed to overcome all of these issues and deliver the game on schedule. 

Back to office
The release of the Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg on 22 May coincided with public transport being available again, so on the 25th of May, we again started to work from the office. It is really convenient in terms of communication and coordination of actions. It does consume some time to get to the office, but at least you have some boundaries between work and home environments. Also, there is no better time to think about the project than on your way to the office, or back home. 

New challenges
Getting back to the office was far from the end of our adventures. Working together meant following all the safety procedures, like wearing masks in public places and transport, making sure to use antiseptics, etc. We still follow all the rules and try to do whatever we can to minimize the risk of catching a virus or spreading it to our colleagues. That worked well enough throughout the summer. 

Autumn comes, people get ill
In October one of the guys on our team caught the virus, so we immediately offered all the team to work remotely until things settle. Several other people on the team have also gotten ill but with some regular illnesses, and our marketing manager even had to go through an appendectomy. All of that came at about the same time, which was highly unfortunate. 

Additionally, the person in charge of the VO organization and supervision got ill right during the VO period. Fortunately, this was not COVID, but it was one more setback for our VO production.

Later, the actress doing the female units voices also got ill, so we had to record a week before release in the end. Fortunately, all the cinematics VO sessions were finished during the summer.

By the skin of our teeth
By the end of October, we finally got back to the office, and fortunately had no more serious illnesses on the team. Yet, the time was short, and making all the recently recorded VO game-ready, delivering all localizations and lots of other things was really hard to do in time for the planned 13 November release. We were able to provide the press with early access to the game only 5 days before the release, which is certainly not enough. Yet, during the release itself, we managed to deliver all the core content. Overall, we are happy with the result and that we were able to keep our promise and deliver a solid game on time. 

Better quality at Spectre of Communism release
Despite all the adversities, Spectre of Communism was running quite smoothly at release. While there were some issues, and some minor problems are still getting fixed, judging by your feedback and by the amount of post-release patches, it seems that the game was much more solid at release this time around. There seem to be many more problems during the Blitzkrieg launch. We quickly addressed those issues, and are thankful to you for supporting us and reporting all the problems, allowing us to timely fix them. 

The work continues
We have fixed most of the issues you have reported in Spectre of Communism, and have already started working on the upcoming Strategic Mind: Fight for Freedom title, which is scheduled for Q2 2020. We keep working from the office, however, the situation in Ukraine has deteriorated threateningly over the course of autumn, and there are talks about some form of lockdown in January. So, we consider the possibility of going remote once again for some time, if such need arises. 

Financial results
In the next issue of Developers’ Diaries, we will share some insights into the sales of Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism.

Stay tuned for more Developers’ Diaries next week.

Support our team by adding the next project to your wishlist:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1381850/Strategic_Mind_Fight_for_Freedom/
With best regards
Starni Games team

notes.title: New units in Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism #10
notes.content:
Ilyushin Il-4 (DB-3F)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/24e8772cb41f0ea3593af5b2cd29373bb150385b.png

A modification of earlier DB-3 bomber models. Despite being far from the best design as of 1941, these long-range bombers did perform several daring raids on Berlin in the summer of 1941, proving to Germans that their homeland could also suffer from war. Overall, more than 6000 planes of different modifications were built.

Petlyakov Pe-2

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/e9876bb4514b9817a2ccab1463e298366f2a069c.png

A twin-engined Soviet dive bomber, Pe-2 is considered one of the best aircraft models the USSR produced during the war. Its production numbers went over 11 000 units built.

The Pe-2 was designed in a prison design bureau (sharashka); Vladimir Petlyakov (head engineer) had been arrested and imprisoned in 1937 for allegedly delaying design work on the Tupolev ANT-42 bomber. Petlyakov was given the task of designing a high-altitude fighter, which he successfully accomplished. However, operational experience in the Soviet-Finnish War of 1939-1940 showed that this was not what the Soviet Air Force needed, and Lavrentiy Beria, head of the NKVD and of the sharashka system, ordered that the fighter be redesigned as a dive bomber, with the promise that Petlyakov and his colleagues would be released on its successful completion. The resulting aircraft, the Pe-2 proved to be one of the most successful designs of World War II.

Petlyakov was released in 1940, and was awarded a Stalin Prize in 1941. However, at Kazan, Petlyakov faced increasing difficulties, with many of his trained technicians and machinists conscripted into the Soviet military and sent to the front lines, which adversely affected the aircraft production. He protested to Soviet senior leadership, and was on his way to Moscow in January 1942 (flying in a Pe-2), when he died in an air crash near Arzamas.

notes.title: New units in Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism | Part 8

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/387b1c48654675a4a69a16db9c71e75cdfa3387d.jpg
Glory to the artillery and mortar crews of the Red Army! 

ISU-152

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/e7d88f64fe0bac29cd1d9be75aa9c1d2fccbbf06.jpg

ISU-152 assault gun is the next generation of Soviet assault artillery based on the IS tanks chassis that entered service in 1943. It was unofficially nicknamed Zveroboy (Russian: Зверобой; "beast killer") in response to several large German tanks, including Tigers and Panthers. It was armed with a 152.4 mm ML-20S gun-howitzer. It proved to be successful both as mobile artillery and as an anti-tank weapon. A total of 4,635 units were built.

ISU-122

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/c7107125081e38e436e0bebba34718f97b063a42.jpg

ISU-122 entered service later, in 1944. It had a smaller caliber but was faring better against the enemy armor. The ISU-122 name is an acronym of Iosif Stalin-based - Samokhodnaya Ustanovka (self-propelled gun) 122. A total of 2,410 were built.

While both ISU-152 and ISU-122 were suitable for artillery and anti-tank roles, the ISU was generally used as artillery, and ISU-122 was more widely used in an anti-tank weapon role. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/487270b7c7475339976dbe48893c18545d218bd6.jpg

Hello guys!

With only one day left before the release, we would like to tell you more about the winter operations in the upcoming Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism. 

Where it all started
In Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg we had the German drive towards Moscow. However, it was set in November and at first, there were heavy rains, then Rasputitsa followed, and only later the Frost would set in freezing all the rounds and solving the issue of Rasputitsa. At the same time, it was only the first snow, which melted quickly and would not result in thick snow until later into the winter. All other operations were spring to autumn. 

Winter is coming!
In the upcoming Spectre of Communism title, we added a number of winter operations, including the Battle of Moscow set in December 1941, where you have to make sure the Germans do not end up storming the Kremlin. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/890886e2b0e24efc449c879dce91072b4834482f.jpg

The Winter War 
The toughest winter operation is probably the Winter War against Finland. Only here, Frost effect changes to a Severe frost, which applies penalty even for units with Winter equipment. While units without the winterized equipment have their movement points reduced to a maximum of 1 on top of other penalties. So, it is crucial to supply all of your ket units with proper equipment in this operation and be ready that Severe frost will slow down the latter part of the operation.

notes.title: Update 3.05 “Undo”
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/bf1e4e970f1d5de48596b8237f294777e1599c19.png

Admiral!

Today we bring Strategic Mind: The Pacific up to date with the upcoming Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism title. We introduce a most-wanted feature, judging by the volume of players’ requests for it, the Undo move button.

Undo move
Added the “Undo move” button. It allows you to retrace your unit's last movement. It is eligible, only if you want to change your last movement and the movement did not affect the current tactical situation. It is not eligible if: an attack happened, the spotting has changed, the objective status has changed, the unit embarked/disembarked, etc.

Optimization 
We are working on optimizing the game performance. So, far we successfully implemented a number of improvements. Some are still underway and will be added in future updates, as we keep working on the Strategic Mind series.

Other changes
This changelog is not an exhaustive list of changes, some minor improvements in other areas were also made, some bugs were fixed, and some localization inaccuracies corrected.
We have also added the widgets of the other games of the Strategic Mind series. While some of you may feel unhappy about it, please, bear in mind that it is the only 100% reliable way for us to let you know about the new title coming up. 

We look forward to more feedback from you!

With best regards
Starni Games team

notes.title: 2 days left! New units in Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism part 7
notes.content:
BM-13 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38153924/19a20a6698b8604b149cae464736980b52cd401f.png

Katyusha multiple rocket launcher is a type of rocket artillery first built and fielded by the Soviet Union in World War II. It was a surprise for the Germans early into the war in 1941, however, they did not consider it a big threat. Only massive Katyusha fire, the USSR troops adopted in 1943 cand later, turned out to be the effective way to employ this weapon. 

The BM-13 model was usually mounted on top of the ZIS truck. 

BM-13N

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38153924/c48ef5bddccb0eb42bb7ba3dfb9bf1e7f27172f6.png

The improved BM-13N model was usually mounted on the US lend-lease Studebaker US6 trucks. There were other modifications, like BM 31, also on Studebaker chassis, but with larger caliber rockets. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38153924/b4935ab83f1aebdfedeb4de5933cfa58efdf0401.png

Katyusha MLRs have become a part of folklore, making popular the Russian song about a girl named Katyusha (Russian name). It was considered an instrumental weapon of Soviet victory. Although it’s precision left much to be desired, the massed Katyusha’s fire had, according to many accounts, a devastating effect on the German troops’ morale. 

In the game, Katyusha rocket launchers, have quite low attack values, but they can attack two times every turn and move 3 hexes away after each attack. Combined with high mobility, that makes Katyusha MLRs a very versatile tool. We had MB-13 in our previous titles, but we added two more models, adjusted their stats, and added special skills. So, now this is a much more potent instrument of war. 

We will keep posting new units that will appear for the first time in the Strategic Mind series, so stay tuned!

With best regards
Starni Games team

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/af830035e334ab91b719e9bcc854e04714c45aa4.png
Here is probably the most asked-for feature of the Strategic Mind Series - the “Undo” button.

We have been working hard on implementing this feature that is called to help players how miss clicked during the movement. Before starting to work on it, we asked the community its thoughts on how it should work in this thread.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/d0adc0bde75f6e2bc9bb3b6eb09bf93f544cec0b.png

Summarizing the players’ feedback we got the following features of the Undo button:
1. It reverts the only movement.
2. It is ineligible if anything of the following happens:

 Any attack has happened (including overwatch etc)
 The objectives were affected
 The unit has embarked or disembarked

The implementation was very tricky and gave us all sorts of headaches, like these:

Despite all the difficulties, we are on the finishing line right now, and the Undo button is finally ready for release.

notes.title: Historical personalities in Spectre of Communism | Part 6
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/ee5f4bb9c03c2e9a98b1b2e4d7c33c7aa488454f.png

By seizing the formerly little-known Height 102.0 – the Mamayev Hill - the Red Army fought its way to the fascists' den – Berlin. We are proud to say that our victory in Stalingrad radically changed the whole situation in the Second World War. And this victory meant that our Motherland had withstood one of the most difficult tests in its history. (c)  Aleksandr Vasilevsky

Summary
Aleksandr Mikhaylovich Vasilevsky was one of the best Soviet commanders over the course of WW2. One could argue who was the top commander, but officially, Vasilevsky was recognized as the number 2 commander after Zhukov - he was receiving all the top awards shortly after him. Additionally, he was arguably the best USSR strategist. His unofficial ranking as a number 2 commander made him most likely replacement for Zhukov, should he fall out of Stalin’s favor.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/a186f86f34f39d6a2293541ffee4946aade59cff.png

Family
As a senior officer, Vasilevsky met frequently with Joseph Stalin. During one of these meetings, Stalin asked Vasilevsky about his family. Since Vasilevsky's father was a priest and thus a potential "enemy of the people", Vasilevsky said that he had ended his relationship with them in 1926. Stalin, surprised, suggested that he reestablish his family ties at once, and help his parents with whatever needs they might have.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31809087/cd69a9b9c92a5563d746637da074c82b526dbda1.png

Visit to Germany in November 1940
Accompanied Molotov and the Soviet delegation in a diplomatic visit to Germany in November 1940 for negotiations. Many historians think that the German dissatisfaction with the results of the negotiations was one of the key factors that led to the German attack in June 1941. 


A man who knew his job as he spent a long time commanding a regiment and who earned great respect from everybody. (c) Georgy Zhukov about Vasilevsky

notes.title: Developers' Diaries #4
notes.content:
This summer we have released the Strategic Mind Franchise Soundtrack that will contain all the music for the Strategic Mind series (with the exception of the majority of The Pacific tracks), and all the money we gain from selling it is going into the creation of new tracks.

Why no The Pacific tracks?
The issue with music in Strategic Mind: The Pacific is that we bought music with a 1 commercial product license, and it’s not unique. It may be great music and fit the game, but other projects can use it as well, and we can only use it in one product. There are only 4 tracks written by an individual composer that are available in the Strategic Mind Franchise Soundtrack. 

Why create our own music?
After we realized the issue above, we found a group of composers united under the name of Daraba Studio, who are now in charge of composing and recording all the music for our projects. Starting from Blitzkrieg we own all commercial rights and therefore can release all tracks in a separate soundtrack etc. Additionally, we are always hard-pressed on budget, so creating a separate soundtrack is a great way to add more tracks into the game than originally planned. Finally, we have read a number of users’ requests for a soundtrack, and that is what finally tipped the balance in favor of this new approach. 

How is our progress so far?
The community is quite supportive of the Soundtrack idea, and we thank you for that. So far, we have gathered enough funds from Soundtrack sales to order additional 3 tracks that will be added to the existing soundtrack along with all the Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism tracks that we created using our default budget. All community-funded tracks will have a [Community supported] tag in their name, so you could tell which tracks were added owing to your support.

What are our future plans?
We hope that more players will buy the soundtrack during the Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism release, and it will help us create more Community supported tracks for the next project. If the soundtrack sales would exceed our expectations, we could create some additional tracks for Spectre of Communism and add them to the project when they are ready with one of the updates. 

Adding historical tracks
In Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg we started experimenting with historical music. The problem with it is that there is no copyright on the old music composition (it expired), but there is copyright for the old music performance(recording). That means we have to record our own version of the old songs and music. We do not have the budget for the chorus, so we create only instrumentals. In Blitzkrieg we added 2 tracks to see how they fit the game:

Wenn die Soldaten:
[previewyoutube=Hxp07uxJic0;full][/previewyoutube]
White Army, Balck Baron (aka “The Red Army is the Strongest”):
[previewyoutube=DdzaN9lSasM;full][/previewyoutube]
We were satisfied with the result, so we decided to continue adding some percentage of the tracks of old times in the next titles.

Historical tracks in Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism
Here is the Soviet Air Force March: 
[previewyoutube=g7EGetVNaX0;full][/previewyoutube] 
We also plan to add “The Internationale” and “Korobeiniki”. Additionally, one of the three community-supported tracks will be “Oh Fields, My Fields”. 

Cinematic tracks
We also create special cinematic tracks, that are usually up to 1 minute long and are used only in cinematics. Here are some new cinematic tracks from Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism.

Zhukov theme:
[previewyoutube=bKhYShXu1vI;full][/previewyoutube]
Battle theme:
[previewyoutube=Yt546nKbkdk;full][/previewyoutube]
Gameplay tracks
Gameplay tracks are played at random during the actual gameplay. We will use the tracks from Blitzkrieg and the new tracks. Additionally, this time we want to try and use some of the historic tracks in the gameplay tracks capacity and are eager to hear your feedback.

Soundtrack update
We will update the Strategic Mind Franchise Soundtrack on the Spectre of Communism release date so that all current and future owners will get access to new tracks as well. 

Your feedback and support
Your feedback is very important to us. It is actually you who suggested creating a soundtrack as a separate entity, we just built on that idea. Your thoughts about music quality and its nature are invaluable to us, so make sure you do share your thoughts on our community hubs and in the comments below. Also, every soundtrack purchase makes us one step closer to adding yet another track into the series. So, we greatly appreciate your support.

We will post the next issue of the Developers’ Diaries as soon as we can, so stay tuned. 

With best regards
Starni Games team

notes.title: New units in Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism | Part 5
notes.content:
IS-3

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38153924/cb896532e8a0deafddce570a7d974801a05b4580.png

We have already talked about IS-2 (The IS acronym is the anglicized initialism of Joseph Stalin (Ио́сиф Ста́лин, Iosif Stalin) before. Now we will proceed to its successors. It had certain engineering novelties, such as the cone-shaped frontal part of the hull. The idea was to improve defense, but in fact, it made a production process more complicated and the effectiveness was questionable. So, in the next IS-4 model that change was reverted. Overall, IS-3 had more armor than its predecessor, making it one of the heaviest tanks of the time. 

IS-4

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38153924/c73a0d35171ba3eb08140e4b5b8278e70a4edc34.png

IS-4 had even more armor than IS-4. However, it turned out that additional planting had little effect: the guns that could not harm IS-3, still could not do it, but the guns that were able to penetrate IS-3 armor, could penetrate the reinforced planting of IS-4 as well. Combined with the growing power of top anti-tank guns, it was unrealistic to create an impenetrable tank in 1945. The reputation of KV tanks in 1941 as being nearly impossible to kill, was largely due to the fact that the German army lacked powerful anti-tank guns at the time. 

The main armament of the IS-2, IS-3, and IS-4 tanks was a solid 122-mm gun D-25T.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38153924/0350c7b8d123b2c71548099ec2f7732c8cde7dd4.png

We will keep posting new units that will appear for the first time in the Strategic Mind series, so stay tuned!

With best regards
Starni Games team

notes.title: New units in Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism | Part #4
notes.content:
SU-122

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38153924/b707115fb6ce4d527770af8731e644f0f4da0d5e.png

In Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg, we introduced new unit classes, one of them being the Assault guns. Now, we present to you the Soviet units of this class. 

When Soviet troops met the German StuGs on the battlefield, the question of implementing similar design ideas was raised. 

To minimize development and production time, as well as, minimize potential design issues, the T-34 tank chassis was picked for the new vehicle. The T-34 tanks have proven to be a very reliable and durable model, so picking their chassis for SU-122 was only logical. In the end, the Red Army got a powerful and mobile 122-mm Assault Gun. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38153924/83d25b94beed69f5313c197d443cb0b6f0a91672.png

SU-152

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38153924/8e5358d8d0b8fbe695db5a152f45cc3bc3d595cf.png

In addition to SU-122, a lager caliber Assult gun SU-152 was developed. It was mounted on a KV-1 chassis and had a 152-mm gun, as well as, thicker armor compared to SU-122.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38153924/37d456635d54609a5a6f9ec63e6a5ece2bfa3681.png

The vehicle was designed as an Assault Gun, but it was often used as a heavy tank destroyer, dealing with Tiger tanks and other heavily armored targets quite efficiently. No wonder it was nicknamed Zveroboy ("Beast Slayer").

We will keep posting new units that will appear for the first time in the Strategic Mind series, so stay tuned!

With best regards
Starni Games team

notes.title: Weekly Intelligence Report #7
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36661203/c7fa78776df3d3802cf381e8246e98a61064674f.png

General!

This time our ever-vigilant intelligence service has gotten its hands on the most urgent information.

Starni Games has shown its true colors 
Last week, Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg got a review article from wargamer.com. In the article, the author claims that “the story directly seeks to support Halder’s myth of the "Clean Wehrmacht", and “As someone who watches the news and sees political upheaval in almost every Western democracy, it is troubling to see a game continue to feed reactionary rhetoric.” 👉 The original article can be found here.

The players’ community has brought this review to our community hub and asked for our opinion. Our COO and person in charge of the narrative supervision - Alexandr - has already shared some thoughts with the community on our forums. 👉 Read the developer's answer.

Afterward, wargamer team member stated in the comments, that the reply “shows their [Starni Games’] true colours somewhat”. 

Usually, we would not react to an article, as we think every reviewer has the right to express their opinion of the game freely. However, in this case, we feel that our company’s reputation is at stake, so we have to make a statement on Starni Games behalf:
«Recently, Starni Games were accused of “supporting Halder’s myth of the 'Clean Wehrmacht”, and “feeding reactionary rhetoric”, by the wargamer.com review written by Jack Trumbull. Basically, it stops short of calling us Nazis outright. For example, “The voice acting [...] in SM:B, but I could say that it is rather generous to fascism, through lines such as 'The trains are running on time' and 'We will save the world from chaos' coming from your Wehrmacht units as they seek to expand the German Reich.” In that regard, we have the following comments:

First, we firmly stand by Freedom of Speech, so we are okay with the article in any form, but we feel obliged to express our own view. 

Second, even though accusations seem wild to us, we feel obliged to ascertain that our company does not support the Nazi or any other “reactionary” ideology. We usually avoid the discussion of our political views, but we can assure you they are far from the “right-wing”.

Third, calling Ukrainian people, who know first-hand about revisionism, territory annexation, and whose country is in the state of unproclaimed war since 2014 a “reactionary” supporters is even more insulting. One of our employees is a refugee from the Donbas region, where the 6-year-long war continues. He would have been the first to throw stones at us, not the wargamer.com review author. In the last 14 years, we had 2 liberty-oriented revolutions in our country, which we ardently supported, so implying we are some sort of “reactionary fascist” is wild and sounds more like a propaganda narrative than a game review to us.

Fourth, we have already explained our take on the “supporting Halder’s myth of the 'Clean Wehrmacht” part on our forums, but here we will provide a quick summary. We do not argue with the existence of the 'Clean Wehrmacht’ myth, it exists. However, the article fails to provide enough evidence of our game supporting that myth. Moreover, we think that our game shows enough of the Germany WW2 war crimes, and as a Commander in Chief of Army, Halder certainly shares responsibility for the political leadership’s decisions. That much was obvious to us, so we thought that it would be apparent to everyone.

Fifth, as we said before on numerous occasions, including the ban of our game in Russia, we stand by the ideas of liberty, freedom of speech, and freedom of creation. The wargamer is free to publish whatever they want, but they accuse us of supporting right/reactionary, etc views which would have been contrary to our company’s values and undermine our reputation.

Sixth, we think that:

 After the US campaign, we could be called “the agents of Uncle Sam”
 After the Japanese campaign, we could be called “faithful servants of the Emperor”
 After the German campaign, we could be called “nazi supporters”
 After the USSR campaign, we could be called “soviet revisionists”
 After the Fight for Freedom release, we could be called “ambassadors of NATO spreading the taint of liberal ideas”

For Gods’ sake, people, we are just creating historical wargames. Of course, everything can be portrayed as if we are in favor of some ideology, but we only try to show every side of the conflict’s sentiment, logic, and convictions, without supporting them, or claiming that “it is the only true path”. We leave all the conclusions to the players.

Seventh, we will keep doing our job of creating games we believe in, disregarding any and all attempts to bring censorship of any kind into our products unless it is a legal request.
»

notes.title: Developers’ Diaries #2
notes.content:
Since Panzer Strategy development we wanted to add unit lines — some things units will say at random commenting on the in-game events.

During the Strategic Mind: The Pacific development we finally had enough voice actors and other resources to fulfill our long-time plan. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/991810/Strategic_Mind_The_Pacific/?beta=0
The units' speech has arrived!

We added over 700 unique lines for the US units and over 700 lines for the Empire of Japan units. 

US units

1. "The US military is the most professional".

[previewyoutube=o3pRc4jk7Oo;leftthumb](unit line)[/previewyoutube]










2. "We stand for democracy".

[previewyoutube=t2GhIuNpyZk;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]










Japan units

1. "What does the Empire want us to do?"

[previewyoutube=fY1zyYGAqHI;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]










2. "My life for the Emperor!"

[previewyoutube=NiRbiCdIV3Y;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]










3. "Imperial Air Service".

[previewyoutube=oizxtT4WwTQ;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]










We strive for diversity

Every class of units had its own set of lines and triggers, like: selection, movement, attack, killing an enemy, forcing the enemy to retreat, low/out of ammo/fuel, enemy spotted, etc. Here are some of them:   

1. "We running out of ammo. Arrows won't fly if the quiver is empty".

[previewyoutube=MMx4sQoscFg;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]










2. "We running out of fuel supplies, Sir".

[previewyoutube=UJfCJ0bM4S8;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]










3. "Enemy down!"

[previewyoutube=_ifzh35ZA9A;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]










Unique in everything!

We had 12 core classes for each side, and a special class — B-29 bombers for the US and kamikaze units for Japan.

B-29 bombers

"Superfortress at your service!"

[previewyoutube=-0BCEaUHmgE;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]










Kamikaze units

"Banzai!"

[previewyoutube=Hw0cP41K9H8;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]










HQ skills

We, also, added lines for HQ skills usage:

1. All guns ready!

[previewyoutube=nfHXmpDFL6A;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]










2. Get ready to fire again!

[previewyoutube=X1JqJRD_p1A;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]










3. Verifying the enemy's location.

[previewyoutube=cad9AmihlkY;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]










Yes, Sir!

We wanted the lines to be quite diverse — not to get repetitive fast. Yet there are only so many military commands, lines like “Yes, Sir”, that would sound 100% natural. 

[previewyoutube=o0se-mEH5Yo;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]










At the same time, hearing “Yes, Sir” all the time sounds really boring. So, we decided to experiment and add a wide range of phrases, some of them of humorous nature. 

[previewyoutube=98z6IUtDqxo;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]










Community feedback

The community reaction varied — many did not like our approach. We think that those who do not like unit lines can switch them off in the options easily, while many other players who, like us, think that these lines bring additional diversity and fun into the game can play with them on and enjoy the game even more. 

From our experience, when you play the game with units’ speech on, quite often there will be moments when the unit’s comment will fit the situation so neatly, that you start to wonder, is it not directed by some sort of AI? These moments are often quite hilarious.

Please, let us know what are your impressions and experience with the unit speech. 

We will tell you more about the units’ speech in Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg in the next issue of our Developers’ Diaries. 

Looking forward to your feedback
Starni Games team

notes.title: Developers’ Diaries #1 by Starni Games
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/891ed0875e18d9564c6a5969679a7d4c61a55a6d.png

Hello guys!

Creating games is a challenging, creative and exciting process.

We decided to share with you what happens behind the scenes in our new series
of articles — Developers’ Diaries by Starni Games.

Recently, we have announced our next project Strategic Mind: Spectre of Communism (to be released in Q4 2020). We are already working full steam on the project. 

Last week we tested a new setup for mocap and sound recording: we tested two different microphones to decide what is the best way to record sound and animation for Spectre of Communism. Additionally, we had to decide whether to switch to an adjusted production process for mocap and VO.

We tested two microphones: stationary studio mic and DPA microphone lavalier. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/63e121069e54d0f8f9c63e16a3ef2c2bbdf982ef.jpg

Microphone lavalier is used on TV and in TV-series if the actor has to move a lot during the recording as it is very convenient and moves with the actor.

Studio stationary mic is used for music recording, podcasts and radio. It is fixed in place and cannot be used by a moving actor.  

Despite the stationary mic providing finer details of the voice, we decided to use the lavalier mic as it offers high quality recording while also allows movement. It is extremely important for us as we will use the motion capture technologies to record the movements and facial animations of the actor and then transfer them to the game character. If we use a stationary mic, the sound will drop if the actor turns his head away from the mic to look at the other character. 

Our cinematic director Constantine tries out the some of the motion capture equipment setup:

https://media.giphy.com/media/UqwftHrCQlWx4TyDHK/giphy.gif

Our COO Oleksandr is adjusting the helmet with an attached Iphone, which is used to capture facial animations:

https://media.giphy.com/media/YoQqlob9pYhBTm9ApQ/giphy.gif

Some weird stuff happening during the tests. The good thing is that the issue was quickly solved:

https://media.giphy.com/media/MByYBtFz8FY1nGFuru/giphy.gif

The results of test
We decided to go for a new technical setup.

Old production process
Motion capture + preliminary VO made by one actor for all characters.
All other voice actors had to fit the preliminary VO and lip sync during the final VO. 

Planned production process
Motion capture + final VO at the same time by every actor. We think this way the voice and animation will be a better match. The time will tell. 

We hope that these adjustments and new mic will help us deliver the cinematics of higher quality in the upcoming project.

The VO + mocap sessions will start soon. We will keep you informed about our progress. 

Your Starni Games team

notes.title: Blitzkrieg: two months = 18 updates
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36661203/3e837c08dabc6008c5d5fd083d6f4103158e1cf3.png

We would like to congratulate the players’ community with the 2 months anniversary of Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg.

These two months we work hard to fix all of the reported issues and further improve the game: 18 updates in two months can truly be called “a Blitzkrieg” on its own.
What we have done
Apart from bug fixes, the game went through the following improvements:

 New Equipment added + all equipment balancing 
 Balance changes for the majority of operations
 Steam achievements added:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36661203/bcd6442936692c02a9a0957b05ee2d9d6fa653d0.png
 Naval tutorial added
 Better Steam integration
 You can adjust difficulty after every operation
 Added new terrain type — Street, improving the city-combat part of the gameplay 
 Added option to set a delay after each phrase 0-5 sec
 All new save files are now archived, so they take tenfolds less disk space now
 Added option to set the number of last save files 10-100 — the rest will be deleted automatically
 Slight UI improvements etc.

The majority of these changes were inspired by your feedback which we carefully accumulated and immediately acted upon. We look forward to more feedback from you guys!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36661203/05307cdc55f129234ba6067633d23ef4a7bfada0.png

What we plan to do
The roadmap for the future updates is currently looking like that

 Leaderboards: recording your score and comparing it to the other players globally
 Steam Community Items: trading cards, badges etc.
 The “Undo” button: the ability to correct a misclick, if it did not result in a fight or spotting of the enemy unit.

Strategic Mind: The Pacific update
Another important matter is that most of the important changes were transferred to the Strategic Mind: The Pacific as well. So, all the players of Strategic Mind series can benefit from the improvements. This also means that when the next Strategic Mind title will come out, many important features will be added retrospectively to Strategic MInd: Blitzkrieg as well.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36661203/dc8aad248917bcb5e6201997f2e9d69d433a9745.png

Soundtrack is out

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1358280/Strategic_Mind_Franchise_Soundtrack/

Upcoming project in Strategic Mind series

And last but not least, we have announced our next title — Strategic MInd: Spectre of Communism. It will allow you to witness the WWII events from the opposite side’s perspective. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1341170/Strategic_Mind_Spectre_of_Communism/

Overall, it was busy 2 months, but our tanks are swift and they only gain speed.

There is more news that we are excited to share with you coming up, so stay tuned! 

With best regards
Strani Games team

notes.title: Update 3.00 is now live!
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/1299ab5901cb258182ddeda914bd39350c16d74a.png
Update 3.00

Steam achievements added!
You asked us to add Steam achievements since the game release. It did take us quite a while, but finally, the achievements are live. We hope that you will enjoy the additional reward for the sophisticated and large-scale operations of Strategic Mind: The Pacific.

Steam cloud saves
Finally, your saves files will be stored in the Steam cloud. So, you no longer risk losing them and can easily transfer them to another device.

Better Steam integration

 Now, you can change the language in Steam settings before you launch the game.
 Also, now your Steam language is set as the game language by default.

New set of controls
Now there is a new set of controls ("Modern") set by default. The old controls are now "Legacy" controls. You can change between the two in the Settings->Game->Controls section. 
Modern:
Unit selection - Left mouse button
Attack/Movement - Right mouse button
Open unit info - Middle (wheel) mouse button (or "I" hotkey)
Legacy:
Unit selection - Left mouse button
Attack/Movement - Left mouse button
Open unit info - Right mouse button

Added ground combat tutorials from the Blitzkrieg
Added 5-part tutorial in ground combat, supplied, infrastructure, etc. 

Revamped UI with new features

 Improved design and usability
 You can now enter custom names for your units (and save files)
 You can see the day/night cycle and the current date (icon in the top right corner)
 Improved the Manual UI

New equipment
 Sniper squad
 Molotov cocktail
 Smoke grenade
 Spaced armor
 Searchlights (small, medium, big) 

Equipment changes
Now incendiary bomb/shells and armor-piercing bombs/shells cost 0 Prestige to install on your unit, but instead each time you use them you have to spend:
3 Prestige for an Incendiary shell
5 Prestige for an Armor-piercing shell
5 Prestige for an Incendiary bomb
5 Prestige for an Armor-piercing bomb

Recon units can now use mortars and recoilless guns
Slight changes in various equipment stats and cost

Gameplay changes:
 Reworked AI (it is less "suicidal" now). 
 If the unit has already attacked this turn it cannot change Equipment until the end of turn.
 Reinforcement no longer costs Command points (only Prestige). Prestige cost is now x2 of what you would have had to spend at the end of the operation. (On default settings 40% of unit cost (it was 50% before)). 
 Removed experience cap (per turn) for all units
 Increased the experience required to gain a 2-5th level
 The maximum level for heroes is lowered from 10 to 5 (If you already had high-level heroes they will remain as before with all the skills, but will not be able to level up further. Also, their stats bonus is capped at +5.)
 Now killing an enemy unit with a hero gives +50 Exp instead of +10.

New settings
 You can now set the Unit speech volume separately from other sources
 Fixed disable/enable hex grid option

New hotkeys
 H; Show/hide hex grid
 I; Show Unit info screen of the selected unit
 Alt; Show unit outlines (if disabled)
 F1; Show hotkeys list

Additionally, we fixed a number of bugs and added some other minor improvements along the way. 

We will keep updating and supporting Strategic Mind: The Pacific as well as other titles of the Strategic Mind series. We are working on Polish localization and plan to add it soon. 

We hope that we will enjoy playing the revamped version of the game. If there are still some issues left unfixed - make sure to let us know on the community hub. 

With best regards
Starni Games development team

notes.title: Blitzkrieg vs The Pacific
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/133b41bf05bc69361030eda14a7a57f49b92c494.png
Today, a day before the release, we want to look back at the production process and compare Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg with Strategic Mind: The Pacific. Let us look into what key features and improvements were added in the second installment of the project.
Core content:

 The campaign consists of 20 large operations offering over 80 hours of gameplay in a straight playthrough. (It is more the both US and Japanese campaigns from The Pacific put together)
 90 minutes of in-game cinematics
 Better narrative integration (eg. objectives to deal with enemy heroes)
 More detailed tutorials

Game mechanics:

 Refined the existing set of core mechanics
 Added two new player-controlled classes of units with their respective skill sets. (Assault guns and Armored trains)
 Added new skills and equipment
 Added more weather effects
 More HQ skills (including V-1 Flying bomb)

Graphics:

 New visuals close in style to The Pacific but adjusted for the European theatre of operations
 New unit models
 More visual changes tied to day/night cycle (Light in the houses, searchlights, etc)

Cinematics:

 Improved motion capture technology and pipeline
 Outdoor scenes created with photo scans usage
 Improved character models

User interface:

 Full revamp of the UI
 A new set of controls and other new game settings
 Custom names for units (and saves)
 More hints and interactive elements
 More hotkeys

Additional features:

 Steam Cloud support
 Nvidia Geforce NOW support
 Text localization for 8 languages (It was 6 at the Strategic Mind: The Pacific release)


Many of these changes will be retrospectively added into Strategic Mind: The Pacific with the upcoming update. 

The release date for Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg is 22 May 2020 at 12.00 PM PDT (21.00 CEST). We look forward to seeing you in-game and on our Community hub. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1200330/Strategic_Mind_Blitzkrieg/

With best regards
Starni Games development team

notes.title: Players feedback inspired features in Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg
notes.content:
Since the Panzer Strategy release in 2018, we were gathering lots of valuable feedback from the players. Some things we could implement fast, for others we had to do extensive preliminary work. Thus, we always note what the players ask for and try to implement it as soon as we have the opportunity.  

Strategic Mind: The Pacific development allowed us to implement many (but not all) of the community suggestions both from Panzer Strategy and from The Pacific early access period. Among the new features, added due to your feedback were:
Detailed combat prediction window
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/054d49d2f678a08158ff2ad7030b9c00ab95d452.png
Many hints, explanations, and Manual (far from perfect, but a good start)
Terrain and infrastructure info
Naval combat tutorial
Further camera zoom option.
Units speech, zoom-in on unit renders, and others.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/9f8d6b45ca9c7cbdb3e73230cf73c7a8e48a2849.png
However, there were still more things that we wanted to implement but they required more time and preparations. So, we got some of them ready for the Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg release, namely:
You can now rename your units with custom names. (and the save files)
You can two choose between two sets of Controls: Modern (new) and Legacy (old). 
Modern (Unit selection - Left mouse button, Attack/Movement - Right mouse button, Open unit info screen - Middle mouse button (or I hotkey, or left-click on corresponding UI button))
Legacy (Unit selection - Left mouse button, Attack/Movement - Left mouse button, Open unit info screen - Right mouse button (or I hotkey, or left-click on corresponding UI button))
Added detailed 5-part tutorial for land operations
UI polish and improvements


Added calendar button indication Day/Night cycle
You can turn on/off the hex grid not only in the Settings but also with the H hotkey.
Added a separate setting for unit speech volume.
Improved Manual UI (We will keep improving it further in the future)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/14c0d699e4779fbd4ed3d2e821e16383c0de0339.png

All these features were brought by a combination of you being interested in our games, actively sending us lots of feedback and great suggestions, and by our willingness to listen to the community and improve our games together. We will keep adding new features and polishing the existing ones. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34062974/13798723daed29a474e25e265a7562f05fd9e205.png

There are still many features that we want to add, but up to now lacked the time and resources to implement. The top two things on our “to-do” list right now are the integration of Steam cloud saves and Steam achievements. No ETA on these, but we will surely add them as soon as we can. 

Do not forget to wishlist Strategic Mind: Blitzkrieg to show us your interest in the project and stay tuned for more information about new content and game development progress.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1200330/Strategic_Mind_Blitzkrieg/

With best regards
Starni Games development team

notes.title: Update 2.06
notes.content:
In today’s update 2.06 we fix more issues reported by the community and improved German localization.

Changes:
 Corrected all German “technical localization” (all the abilities, ship parts descriptions, etc.) There might still be some things to fix with the new version, which we will address in later updates, but over we expect the quality of localization to increase dramatically. Next, we will work on fixing German subtitles for cinematics. If you play the game with German localization on, please do let us know what you think about these fixes.
 We made some changes to the Australia deployment phase: now you have only 4 deploy hexes in each location, representing the fact that not the whole fleet was able to reach Australia in time. You can deploy the rest of your units in the second deploy phase before turn 2. Additionally, we moved some of the enemy forces further away to balance out the increase in the difficulty of the objective to cover the Army landing. 
 Adjusted the stats of Japanese Ground transports, as some of them were incorrect. Additionally, the USA Ground transport LVT-4 now adds 2 Soft attack and 1 Hard attack as it had guns mounted on it.
 Fixed an occasional tutorial issue when the player could not press the “Acquire” button (Reported by ChiefCommander33, and others). (It was quite hard to replicate, as it was not happening on any of the PCs in our office. Luckily, one of our friends has encountered it on her laptop and allowed us to borrow it for a few days. Even then it was hard to figure it out). 
 Fixed important crash (reported by [CHN]Zephyr), which was happening after an Infantry unit spent all its movement points, then got new Ground transport, and it could still move on the transport causing a crash. Another variant of the same issue was crash after the Infantry with transport got overrun and was shown ineligible hexes to move to, and if the player chose to move there the game would crash.
 Fix an issue with Japanese campaign 05 operation (reported by Nix), where completing objectives in a certain order would cause a crash.
 Fix an issue with Japanese campaign 05 operation, the objective to pursue the enemy fleet was working incorrectly.
 Fixed USA campaign 04 operation secondary objective to kill submarines not giving experience to your Destroyers as a part of the reward. (Reported by Tim)
 Fixed USA campaign 06 operation secondary objective to capture the place where Marines barracks were not giving experience to your Marines as a part of the reward. (Reported by The Matrix has you!)
 Fixed Japan campaign 05 operation secondary objective to prevent Zero capture, the turn timer was going up instead of going down.
 Fixed a rare bug in Japanese campaign 08 operation, where you would fail secondary objective even if you captured oil storages. (Reported by aramoor50, thank you for the save files)
 Fixed some visual elements on the map (eg. railroad on bridges etc) on several maps. 
 Fixed incorrect text in Japanese campaign 06 operations the secondary objective “capture the airfield at Munda” -> “Hold the airfield at Munda”. (Reported by Night_Phoenix)
 Fixed dialogue when first attacking Tekketsu Kinotai in USA campaign operation 09. 
 In the Japanese campaign 06 operation we moved the completion of the main objective to hold all victory hexes one turn earlier so that you do not get a warning that you have the last turn before indecision penalty kicks in even though you did everything perfectly.

We would like to thank all of our community members who keep reporting all the occurring issues and help us to make the game better. We do appreciate your help. Additionally, we would like to thank Night Phoenix for his Lets play series covering the Japanese campaign, as it also helped us to identify and fix a couple of issues. 

We will keep improving and polishing the game. Our team wishes everyone good holidays. Stay tuned as there are some big announcements coming. 

With best regards
Starni Games development team
